findings.finding: Stronger or off the observings: 'keeping' and 'neighbours' dissolved; 'however near or far' dissolved and 'nearest birds' contradicts regardless of distance; the firefly is one observing, not 'a synchronous firefly ... pauses', and 'seeing a partner's flashing' is added; pigeon influence is faithfulness of its own solo route, not 'goes its own route'; collapse was of tracking, not all orienting; strider prey ripples, not 'the surface's'.
findings.proposed_new: A lone golden shiner moves almost at random. In a school, each fish responds only to the brightness at its own place, slowing in the dark, and moves close to the fish around it; a larger school reliably goes toward shade, slowing and bunching inside it and speeding up to leave as light moves onto it, and a school below a certain size loses its tracking of the shade. Larger pigeon flocks fly significantly shorter routes than smaller flocks, and a flock's route is not simply the average of its birds' routes: each pigeon's influence on the route is in proportion to how faithfully it reproduces its own route in solo flights. In flocks of a few thousand, each bird interacts with about six or seven other birds, the same number at each distance between them. In one observing, a Photuris frontalis firefly pauses for 3.0 to 24.1 seconds, then resumes at once, synchronous with its partner. A water strider senses the ripples of prey with its front legs, and each species shares its own surface waves in courtship and in a territory.

A network of resolvers is a same-existing-society, its orienting in no self alone.

findings.finding: 'onsets 4 ms apart being enough' adds a sufficiency the observing does not give; the 0.1 and the halving of the factor are lost.
findings.proposed_new: A Cupiennius spider always moves toward the legs a vibration reaches first, onsets 4 ms apart, or toward the legs it reaches with larger amplitude; a vibration reaching a front leg lowers the weighting of the legs behind it on its own side by 0.1, and with vibration reaching both sides this lowering goes front to back alone and halves the factor. Its turning error grows as the source is further behind it.

findings.finding: Eight legs are two sides by four along, not 2x2x2, and 'first or not first' is not a leg; co-parity and bi-parity (Naming 2.5, dimensions 3 and 4) are collapsed into 'agree or part now' and a turning is not the next same-existing self-parity; 'a sequencing and no timing' contradicts the 4 ms onset; 'two of every three' uses every.
findings.proposed_new: Eight legs are two sides across and four legs along each side, two times four being eight. Each leg opens with its own prior self-parity and its partner leg's prior other-parity across; now its co-parity and bi-parity agree or part; and its next same-existing self-parity is the spider's turning: five dimensions, a vibration coming inward along the legs and a turning going outward. Its direction resolves by which legs change first, onsets 4 ms apart, or by the larger amplitude on its legs. An octopus has eight arms and two of each three of its neurons in them, an arm tasting semi-independently.

findings.proposed_new: Navigating hard problems of science are observed here as this five-dimensional, two-directional navigating, possibling with bi-moral co-agency: monarchs orient by a time-compensated sun compass and a light-dependent magnetic inclination compass; green sea turtles in a pool, in the field of a place about 209 miles north of their capture site, swim south, toward the capture site; in bird magnetoreception, radical pairs in cryptochrome photoexcited in the retina are the leading hypothesis, its mechanism unclear; six of 21 eels with tags reach the Sargasso Sea. Any animal's sensing of the magnetic field is a possibling, its mechanism open.
